# Install fake docker-compose wrapper if not present
if ! command -v docker-compose >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! docker-compose exec -T mysql_test mysql -uroot -ptoor -e "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    cat > /usr/local/bin/docker-compose << 'WRAPPER'
#!/bin/bash
action="$1"
shift
if [ "$action" = "exec" ]; then
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            -T) shift ;;
            mysql_test|mysql_replica_test)
                shift
                exec mysql -h127.0.0.1 -P3307 "$@"
                ;;
            *) shift ;;
        esac
    done
    exit 1
else
    exit 0
fi
WRAPPER
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/docker-compose
fi

# Ensure MySQL is running on port 3307
if ! mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3307 -u root -ptoor -e "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Starting MySQL on port 3307..."
    mkdir -p /var/run/mysqld && chown mysql:mysql /var/run/mysqld
    mysqld --user=mysql --port=3307 --bind-address=127.0.0.1 --socket=/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock --pid-file=/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.pid &
    sleep 3
    mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3307 -u root -e "ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'toor'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Ensure Redis is running
if ! redis-cli ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Starting Redis..."
    redis-server --daemonize yes --port 6379
    sleep 1
fi

    echo "Generating bindata..."

fi

# Run the MDM integration tests
export MYSQL_TEST=1
export REDIS_TEST=1

cd /testbed
go test -tags full,fts5,netgo -vet=off -v -run=TestIntegrationsMDM/TestInvalidCommandUUID ./server/service/ -timeout=10m -count=1

+from concurrent.futures import Future
+import inspect
+import unittest
+
+from opcua import Server, ua
+from opcua.common import event_objects
+from opcua.common.event_objects import BaseEvent
+
+
+class _EventRecorder:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.future = Future()
+
+    def datachange_notification(self, node, val, data):
+        pass
+
+    def event_notification(self, event):
+        self.future.set_result(event)
+
+
+class TestEventEmitterConstruction(unittest.TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.srv = Server()
+        cls.srv.set_endpoint("opc.tcp://127.0.0.1:48570")
+        cls.srv.start()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        cls.srv.stop()
+
+    def _audit_event_classes(self):
+        classes = []
+        for name in dir(event_objects):
+            if not (name.startswith("Audit") and name.endswith("Event")):
+                continue
+            cls = getattr(event_objects, name)
+            if inspect.isclass(cls) and issubclass(cls, BaseEvent):
+                classes.append(cls)
+        self.assertGreater(len(classes), 10)
+        return classes
+
+    def _new_constructor_option_name(self):
+        legacy_names = {"self", "sourcenode", "message", "severity"}
+        params = inspect.signature(BaseEvent).parameters
+        candidates = [
+            name
+            for name, param in params.items()
+            if name not in legacy_names
+            and param.kind in (param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD, param.KEYWORD_ONLY)
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            len(candidates),
+            1,
+            "BaseEvent should expose one new public constructor option for the emitting node",
+        )
+        return candidates[0]
+
+    def _construct_with_distinct_emitter(self, cls, described, emitter, message=None, severity=1):
+        option_name = self._new_constructor_option_name()
+        return cls(
+            sourcenode=described,
+            message=message,
+            severity=severity,
+            **{option_name: emitter}
+        )
+
+    def _objects_node(self):
+        return self.srv.get_objects_node()
+
+    def _new_object(self, name):
+        return self._objects_node().add_object(2, name)
+
+    def _subscribe_and_trigger(self, subscribed_node, event):
+        recorder = _EventRecorder()
+        sub = self.srv.create_subscription(50, recorder)
+        handle = sub.subscribe_events(subscribed_node)
+        try:
+            event.EventId = b"fixtured-event"
+            self.srv.iserver.isession.subscription_service.trigger_event(event)
+            return recorder.future.result(5)
+        finally:
+            sub.unsubscribe(handle)
+            sub.delete()
+
+    def test_base_event_routes_by_default_server_emitter_without_rewriting_source_node(self):
+        described = self._new_object("FixtureDDefaultSource")
+        event = BaseEvent(sourcenode=described.nodeid)
+
+        received = self._subscribe_and_trigger(self.srv.get_server_node(), event)
+
+        self.assertEqual(described.nodeid, received.SourceNode)
+        self.assertNotEqual(self.srv.get_server_node().nodeid, received.SourceNode)
+
+    def test_base_event_routes_by_constructor_emitter_without_rewriting_source_node(self):
+        described = self._new_object("FixtureDBaseSource")
+        emitter = self._new_object("FixtureDBaseEmitter")
+        emitter.set_event_notifier([ua.EventNotifier.SubscribeToEvents])
+        event = self._construct_with_distinct_emitter(
+            BaseEvent,
+            described.nodeid,
+            emitter.nodeid,
+        )
+
+        received = self._subscribe_and_trigger(emitter, event)
+
+        self.assertEqual(described.nodeid, received.SourceNode)
+        self.assertNotEqual(emitter.nodeid, received.SourceNode)
+
+    def test_base_event_backwards_compatible_existing_arguments(self):
+        described = ua.NodeId(5003, 2)
+        message = "legacy message"
+        severity = 42
+
+        event = BaseEvent(described, message, severity)
+
+        self.assertEqual(described, event.SourceNode)
+        self.assertEqual(message, event.Message.Text)
+        self.assertEqual(severity, event.Severity)
+
+    def test_audit_event_classes_accept_the_same_constructor_option(self):
+        described = ua.NodeId(5004, 2)
+        emitter = ua.NodeId(6004, 2)
+        message = "audit compatibility"
+        severity = 43
+
+        for cls in self._audit_event_classes():
+            event = self._construct_with_distinct_emitter(
+                cls,
+                described,
+                emitter,
+                message=message,
+                severity=severity,
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(described, event.SourceNode, cls.__name__)
+            self.assertNotEqual(emitter, event.SourceNode, cls.__name__)
+            self.assertEqual(message, event.Message.Text, cls.__name__)
+            self.assertEqual(severity, event.Severity, cls.__name__)
+
+    def test_audit_create_session_routes_by_emitter_while_source_is_session_node(self):
+        described = self._new_object("FixtureDAuditSource")
+        emitter = self._new_object("FixtureDAuditEmitter")
+        emitter.set_event_notifier([ua.EventNotifier.SubscribeToEvents])
+        event = self._construct_with_distinct_emitter(
+            event_objects.AuditCreateSessionEvent,
+            described.nodeid,
+            emitter.nodeid,
+        )
+
+        received = self._subscribe_and_trigger(emitter, event)
+
+        self.assertEqual(ua.NodeId(ua.ObjectIds.AuditCreateSessionEventType), received.EventType)
+        self.assertEqual(described.nodeid, received.SourceNode)
+        self.assertNotEqual(emitter.nodeid, received.SourceNode)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":

+import random
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from kor2vec import ContextKor2Vec, Kor2Vec
+
+
+SAMPLED_ROW = "안녕\t나는 반가워\t도라에몽 클로바\n"
+ONE_WORD_SAMPLED_ROW = "안녕\t나는\t도라에몽\n"
+CORPUS_LINE = "안녕 나는 반가워 도라에몽 클로바\n"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def deterministic_cpu_and_quiet_progress(monkeypatch):
+    torch.set_num_threads(1)
+    monkeypatch.setattr("tqdm.tqdm", lambda iterable=None, *args, **kwargs: iterable)
+
+
+def _write_text(path, text):
+    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+    return str(path)
+
+
+def _rounded_embedding_sum(model, sentence="안녕 나는"):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        return round(float(model.embedding(sentence).sum().item()), 6)
+
+
+def _rounded_parameter_sum(model):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        total = sum(param.detach().cpu().sum() for param in model.parameters())
+        return round(float(total.item()), 6)
+
+
+def _parameter_snapshot(model):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        return [param.detach().cpu().clone() for param in model.parameters()]
+
+
+def _parameters_changed(before, model):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        after = [param.detach().cpu() for param in model.parameters()]
+        if len(before) != len(after):
+            return True
+        return any(not torch.equal(old, new) for old, new in zip(before, after))
+
+
+def _embedding_snapshot(model, sentence="안녕 나는"):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        return model.embedding(sentence).detach().cpu().clone()
+
+
+def _embedding_changed(before, model, sentence="안녕 나는"):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        return not torch.equal(before, model.embedding(sentence).detach().cpu())
+
+
+def _assert_embedding_matches(left, right, sentence="안녕 나는"):
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        assert torch.equal(left.embedding(sentence).detach().cpu(), right.embedding(sentence).detach().cpu())
+
+
+def _assert_sample_file_shape(path, positive_sample_count, negative_sample_count, source_words):
+    rows = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+    assert rows != []
+    for row in rows:
+        fields = row.split("\t")
+        assert len(fields) == 3
+        center, positive, negative = fields
+        positives = positive.split(" ") if positive else []
+        negatives = negative.split(" ") if negative else []
+        assert center in source_words
+        assert len(positives) == positive_sample_count
+        assert len(negatives) == negative_sample_count
+        assert all(word in source_words for word in positives)
+        assert all(word in source_words for word in negatives)
+
+
+def _load_model(path):
+    try:
+        return torch.load(str(path), map_location={"cuda:0": "cpu"}, weights_only=False)
+    except TypeError:
+        return torch.load(str(path), map_location={"cuda:0": "cpu"})
+
+
+def test_kor2vec_train_from_sample_pre_sequence_updates_same_object_and_checkpoints(tmp_path):
+
+
+
+
+    sample_path = _write_text(tmp_path / "sampled.txt", SAMPLED_ROW)
+    out = tmp_path / "kor2vec.pt"
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1337)
+    model = Kor2Vec(embed_size=8)
+
+    before_params = _parameter_snapshot(model)
+    before_embedding = _embedding_snapshot(model)
+
+    result = model.train(
+        sample_path=sample_path,
+        model_path=str(out),
+        positive_sample_count=2,
+        negative_sample_count=2,
+        batch_size=1,
+        epochs=2,
+        pre_sequence=True,
+    )
+
+    assert result is None
+    assert sorted(path.name for path in tmp_path.iterdir()) == [
+        "kor2vec.pt.ep0",
+        "kor2vec.pt.ep1",
+        "sampled.txt",
+    ]
+
+    assert _parameters_changed(before_params, model)
+    assert _embedding_changed(before_embedding, model)
+
+    manual_save = tmp_path / "kor2vec-after-train.pt"
+    model.save(str(manual_save))
+    loaded = _load_model(manual_save)
+
+    _assert_embedding_matches(loaded, model)
+
+
+def test_kor2vec_train_from_sample_lazy_conversion_matches_eager_state(tmp_path):
+
+
+
+
+    sample_path = _write_text(tmp_path / "sampled.txt", SAMPLED_ROW)
+    out = tmp_path / "kor2vec-lazy.pt"
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1337)
+    model = Kor2Vec(embed_size=8)
+    before_params = _parameter_snapshot(model)
+    before_embedding = _embedding_snapshot(model)
+    result = model.train(
+        sample_path=sample_path,
+        model_path=str(out),
+        positive_sample_count=2,
+        negative_sample_count=2,
+        batch_size=1,
+        epochs=2,
+        pre_sequence=False,
+    )
+
+    assert result is None
+    assert sorted(path.name for path in tmp_path.iterdir()) == [
+        "kor2vec-lazy.pt.ep0",
+        "kor2vec-lazy.pt.ep1",
+        "sampled.txt",
+    ]
+
+    assert _parameters_changed(before_params, model)
+    assert _embedding_changed(before_embedding, model)
+
+
+def test_corpus_path_creates_default_sampled_file_and_uses_sampling_counts(tmp_path):
+
+
+
+
+    corpus = tmp_path / "corpus.txt"
+    _write_text(corpus, CORPUS_LINE)
+    out = tmp_path / "corpus-model.pt"
+
+    random.seed(7)
+    torch.manual_seed(1337)
+    model = Kor2Vec(embed_size=8)
+    before_params = _parameter_snapshot(model)
+    result = model.train(
+        corpus_path=str(corpus),
+        model_path=str(out),
+        window_size=3,
+        positive_sample_count=2,
+        negative_sample_count=2,
+        batch_size=1,
+        epochs=1,
+        pre_sequence=False,
+    )
+

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+
+import logging
+
+from pelican.log import LimitFilter
+from pelican.tests.support import unittest
+
+
+def make_record(level, msg, args=()):
+    return logging.LogRecord(
+        name='pelican',
+        level=level,
+        pathname='test',
+        lineno=1,
+        msg=msg,
+        args=args,
+        exc_info=None,
+    )
+
+
+class TestLogFilter(unittest.TestCase):
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+    def setUp(self):
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore = set()
+        LimitFilter._raised_messages = set()
+        LimitFilter._group_count.clear()
+
+
+        self.root = logging.getLogger()
+        self._old_level = self.root.level
+        self.root.setLevel(logging.WARNING)
+        self.f = LimitFilter()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        self.root.setLevel(self._old_level)
+        LimitFilter._ignore = set()
+        LimitFilter._raised_messages = set()
+        LimitFilter._group_count.clear()
+
+
+
+    def test_filter_by_formatted_message_author(self):
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'AUTHOR_SAVE_AS is set to False'))
+        rec = make_record(
+            logging.WARNING, '%s is set to %s',
+            ('AUTHOR_SAVE_AS', 'False'))
+        self.assertFalse(self.f.filter(rec))
+
+    def test_filter_by_formatted_message_category(self):
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'CATEGORY_SAVE_AS is set to False'))
+        rec = make_record(
+            logging.WARNING, '%s is set to %s',
+            ('CATEGORY_SAVE_AS', 'False'))
+        self.assertFalse(self.f.filter(rec))
+
+    def test_filter_by_formatted_messages_combined(self):
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'AUTHOR_SAVE_AS is set to False'))
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'CATEGORY_SAVE_AS is set to False'))
+        rec1 = make_record(
+            logging.WARNING, '%s is set to %s',
+            ('AUTHOR_SAVE_AS', 'False'))
+        rec2 = make_record(
+            logging.WARNING, '%s is set to %s',
+            ('CATEGORY_SAVE_AS', 'False'))
+        self.assertFalse(self.f.filter(rec1))
+        self.assertFalse(self.f.filter(rec2))
+
+
+
+    def test_filter_by_template_still_works(self):
+
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add((logging.WARN, '%s is set to %s'))
+        rec = make_record(
+            logging.WARNING, '%s is set to %s',
+            ('TAG_SAVE_AS', 'False'))
+        self.assertFalse(self.f.filter(rec))
+
+
+
+    def test_unrelated_formatted_message_passes(self):
+
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'AUTHOR_SAVE_AS is set to False'))
+        rec = make_record(
+            logging.WARNING, '%s is set to %s',
+            ('TAG_SAVE_AS', 'False'))
+        self.assertTrue(self.f.filter(rec))
+
+    def test_completely_unrelated_message_passes(self):
+
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'AUTHOR_SAVE_AS is set to False'))
+        rec = make_record(logging.WARNING, 'something totally different')
+        self.assertTrue(self.f.filter(rec))
+
+    def test_filter_no_args_literal_message(self):
+
+
+        LimitFilter._ignore.add(
+            (logging.WARN, 'literal warning text'))
+        rec = make_record(logging.WARNING, 'literal warning text')
+        self.assertFalse(self.f.filter(rec))

+
+def test_replace_recurses_through_since_and_preserves_outer_label() -> None:

+    condition = AutomationCondition.missing().with_label("trigger").since(original_reset).with_label(

+    assert snapshot.children[0].node_snapshot.label is None

+    replacement = AutomationCondition.newly_updated()

+def _make_partition_request(server_url: str, pdf_filename: str) -> httpx.Request:
+    """Build an httpx.Request that mimics what the SDK would send for a partition
+    call with split_pdf_page=true and a multi-page PDF."""
+    with open(pdf_filename, "rb") as f:
+        pdf_content = f.read()
+    encoder = MultipartEncoder(
+        fields={
+            "split_pdf_page": "true",
+            "files": (pdf_filename, pdf_content, "application/pdf"),
+            "strategy": "fast",
+        }
+    )
+    return httpx.Request(
+        "POST",
+        f"{server_url}/general/v0/general",
+        content=encoder.to_string(),
+        headers={"Content-Type": encoder.content_type},
+    )
+
+
+def _make_before_request_context() -> BeforeRequestContext:
+    return BeforeRequestContext(

+    )
+
+
+def test_unit_split_pdf_dummy_request_does_not_use_hardcoded_api_url():
+    """Bug fix: the dummy GET request returned by before_request must not target
+    the hardcoded https://api.unstructuredapp.io URL. Hitting that URL behind a
+    firewall causes the client to hang and time out."""
+    server_url = "http://localhost:9999"
+    hook = SplitPdfHook()
+    hook.sdk_init(base_url=server_url, client=httpx.Client())
+
+    request = _make_partition_request(
+        server_url, "_sample_docs/layout-parser-paper.pdf"
+    )
+    result = hook.before_request(_make_before_request_context(), request)
+
+    assert isinstance(result, httpx.Request)

+    assert "api.unstructuredapp.io" not in str(result.url)
+
+

+    """The dummy GET request should target the user-configured server_url when

+    server_url = "http://localhost:9999"

+import importlib.util
+import sys
+import types
+from datetime import date
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def _load_dmi_module():
+    package = types.ModuleType("middlewared")
+    package.__path__ = [str(Path.cwd() / "src/middlewared/middlewared")]
+    sys.modules["middlewared"] = package
+    service = types.ModuleType("middlewared.service")
+    service.Service = type("Service", (), {"__init__": lambda self, *args, **kwargs: None})
+    service.private = lambda fn: fn
+    sys.modules["middlewared.service"] = service
+    path = Path.cwd() / "src/middlewared/middlewared/plugins/system/dmi.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("middlewared.plugins.system.dmi_contract", path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+def _parse(lines):
+    module = _load_dmi_module()
+    obj = module.SystemService(module.Service)
+    obj.logger = types.SimpleNamespace(warning=lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
+    module.SystemService.CACHE = {key: None for key in module.SystemService.CACHE}
+    module.subprocess.run = lambda *args, **kwargs: types.SimpleNamespace(stdout="\n".join(lines))
+    return obj.dmidecode_info().copy()
+
+
+def test_dmi_parser_keeps_values_in_their_handle_sections_and_aggregates_memory():
+    cache = _parse([
+        "Handle 0x0002, DMI type 2, 15 bytes", "Base Board Information",
+        "        Manufacturer: BoardCo", "        Product Name: Board-1",
+        "Handle 0x0003, DMI type 3, 21 bytes", "Chassis Information",
+        "        Manufacturer: ChassisCo", "        I2C Slave Address: 0x20",
+        "Handle 0x0001, DMI type 1, 27 bytes", "System Information",
+        "        Manufacturer: SystemCo", "        Product Name: Host-1",
+        "        Serial Number: SERIAL", "        Version: v1",
+        "Handle 0x0010, DMI type 16, 23 bytes", "Physical Memory Array",
+        "        Error Correction Type: None",
+        "Handle 0x0011, DMI type 16, 23 bytes", "Physical Memory Array",
+        "        Error Correction Type: Single-bit ECC",
+    ])
+    assert cache == {
+        "bios-release-date": "", "ecc-memory": True,
+        "baseboard-manufacturer": "BoardCo", "baseboard-product-name": "Board-1",
+        "system-manufacturer": "SystemCo", "system-product-name": "Host-1",
+        "system-serial-number": "SERIAL", "system-version": "v1", "has-ipmi": False,
+    }
+
+
+def test_dmi_parser_only_marks_ipmi_for_type_38_records():
+    assert _parse(["Handle 0x0001, DMI type 1, 27 bytes", "System Information",
+                   "        I2C Slave Address: 0x20"])["has-ipmi"] is False
+    assert _parse(["Handle 0x0038, DMI type 38, 18 bytes", "IPMI Device Information",
+                   "        I2C Slave Address: 0x20"])["has-ipmi"] is True
+
+
+def test_dmi_parser_accepts_two_digit_dates_and_ignores_invalid_dates():
+    assert _parse(["Handle 0x0000, DMI type 0, 26 bytes", "BIOS Information",
+                   "        Release Date: 12/03/20"])["bios-release-date"] == date(2020, 12, 3)
+    assert _parse(["Handle 0x0000, DMI type 0, 26 bytes", "BIOS Information",
+                   "        Release Date: not-a-date"])["bios-release-date"] == ""

+class JsonResponse:

+        self.status_code = status_code

+        self.headers = {
+            "content-type": "application/json",

+        }
+        self.text = payload
+        self._payload = payload
+
+    def json(self):
+        return json.loads(self._payload)
+
+
+class CountingSession(requests.Session):
+    active_sessions = 0
+    max_active_sessions = 0
+    close_calls = 0
+
+    def __init__(self, responses=()):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.responses = list(responses)
+        self.posts = []
+        self.closed = False
+        CountingSession.active_sessions += 1
+        CountingSession.max_active_sessions = max(
+            CountingSession.max_active_sessions, CountingSession.active_sessions
+        )
+
+    def post(self, url, **kwargs):
+        self.posts.append((url, kwargs))
+        if not self.responses:
+            raise AssertionError(f"no scripted response for {url}")
+        response = self.responses.pop(0)
+        if isinstance(response, BaseException):
+            raise response
+        return response
+
+    def close(self):
+        if not self.closed:
+            CountingSession.active_sessions -= 1
+            self.closed = True
+        CountingSession.close_calls += 1
+        return super().close()

+package tencentcloud
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+)
+
+
+
+
+func TestIdEncodeDecodeBackwardCompatible(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := [][]string{
+		{"a", "b", "c"},
+		{"apiKeyId", "usagePlanId"},
+		{"single"},
+		{"crs-jf4ico4v", "Keep-terraform"},
+		{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e"},
+	}
+
+	for _, parts := range cases {
+		legacy := strings.Join(parts, "#")
+		assert.Equalf(t, legacy, IdEncode(parts),
+			"IdEncode(%#v) should equal the legacy joined form", parts)
+		assert.Equalf(t, parts, IdDecode(legacy),
+			"IdDecode(%q) should equal the legacy split form", legacy)
+	}
+}
+
+
+func TestIdDecodeLegacy(t *testing.T) {
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{"a", "b", "c"}, IdDecode("a#b#c"))
+	assert.Equal(t, "a#b#c", IdEncode([]string{"a", "b", "c"}))
+}
+
+
+
+
+
+func TestIdEncodeDecodeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := [][]string{
+		{"a#b", "c"},
+		{"a", "b#c", "d"},
+		{"#"},
+		{"##", "#"},
+		{"", "a"},
+		{"a", ""},
+		{"", "", ""},
+		{"a", "", "b"},
+		{`back\slash`, "plain"},
+		{"per%cent", "23"},
+		{"mix#ed\\and%23", "#", "", "tail"},
+		{"crs-jf4ico4v#weird", "Keep-terraform"},
+		{strings.Repeat("#", 5), strings.Repeat("a#", 4)},
+	}
+
+	for _, parts := range cases {
+		encoded := IdEncode(parts)
+		decoded := IdDecode(encoded)
+		assert.Equalf(t, parts, decoded,
+			"round-trip failed for %#v (encoded as %q, decoded as %#v)", parts, encoded, decoded)
+		assert.Lenf(t, decoded, len(parts),
+			"round-trip must preserve the number of fields for %#v", parts)
+	}
+}
+
+
+func TestIdEncodeDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
+	parts := []string{"a#b", "", "c\\d", "#"}
+	assert.Equal(t, IdEncode(parts), IdEncode(parts))
+}

+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+

+
+
+
+
+package node
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+
+	commonv1 "github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/api/proto/banyandb/common/v1"
+	databasev1 "github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/api/proto/banyandb/database/v1"
+	"github.com/apache/skywalking-banyandb/banyand/metadata/schema"
+)
+
+var replicaGroupSchema = schema.Metadata{
+	TypeMeta: schema.TypeMeta{
+		Kind: schema.KindGroup,
+	},
+	Spec: &commonv1.Group{
+		Metadata: &commonv1.Metadata{
+			Name: "rgroup",
+		},
+		Catalog: commonv1.Catalog_CATALOG_MEASURE,
+		ResourceOpts: &commonv1.ResourceOpts{
+			ShardNum: 3,
+		},
+	},
+}
+
+func setupReplicaSelector(nodeNames ...string) Selector {
+	selector := NewRoundRobinSelector("test", nil)
+	selector.(*roundRobinSelector).OnAddOrUpdate(replicaGroupSchema)
+	for _, n := range nodeNames {
+		selector.AddNode(&databasev1.Node{Metadata: &commonv1.Metadata{Name: n}})
+	}
+	return selector
+}
+
+
+func TestReplicaOmittedEqualsPrimary(t *testing.T) {
+	selector := setupReplicaSelector("node1", "node2", "node3")
+	for shardID := uint32(0); shardID < 3; shardID++ {
+		primary, err := selector.Pick("rgroup", "", shardID)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		explicit, err := selector.Pick("rgroup", "", shardID, 0)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		assert.Equal(t, primary, explicit,
+			"picking shard %d without a replica must equal replica 0", shardID)
+	}
+}
+
+
+
+func TestReplicaCopiesAreDistinct(t *testing.T) {
+	nodes := []string{"node1", "node2", "node3"}
+	selector := setupReplicaSelector(nodes...)
+	for shardID := uint32(0); shardID < 3; shardID++ {
+		seen := make(map[string]uint32)
+		for replicaID := uint32(0); replicaID < uint32(len(nodes)); replicaID++ {
+			n, err := selector.Pick("rgroup", "", shardID, replicaID)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			assert.Contains(t, nodes, n)
+			if prev, ok := seen[n]; ok {
+				t.Fatalf("shard %d: replica %d and replica %d both mapped to node %s",
+					shardID, prev, replicaID, n)
+			}
+			seen[n] = replicaID
+		}
+		assert.Len(t, seen, len(nodes),
+			"shard %d: expected %d distinct nodes across its copies", shardID, len(nodes))
+	}
+}
+
+
+
+func TestReplicaSelectionIsDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
+	selector := setupReplicaSelector("node1", "node2", "node3")
+
+	want := make(map[[2]uint32]string)
+	for shardID := uint32(0); shardID < 3; shardID++ {
+		for replicaID := uint32(0); replicaID < 3; replicaID++ {
+			n, err := selector.Pick("rgroup", "", shardID, replicaID)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			want[[2]uint32{shardID, replicaID}] = n
+		}
+	}
+
+
+	for i := 0; i < 50; i++ {
+		for shardID := int(2); shardID >= 0; shardID-- {
+			for replicaID := int(2); replicaID >= 0; replicaID-- {
+				n, err := selector.Pick("rgroup", "", uint32(shardID), uint32(replicaID))
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				assert.Equal(t, want[[2]uint32{uint32(shardID), uint32(replicaID)}], n)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+
+func TestReplicaErrorBehavior(t *testing.T) {
+
+	empty := setupReplicaSelector()
+	_, err := empty.Pick("rgroup", "", 0, 1)
+	assert.Error(t, err, "no nodes available must error for any replica")
+
+	selector := setupReplicaSelector("node1", "node2", "node3")
+
+
+	_, err = selector.Pick("does-not-exist", "", 0, 1)
+	assert.Error(t, err, "unknown group must error for any replica")
+
+
+	_, err = selector.Pick("rgroup", "", 100, 1)
+	assert.Error(t, err, "unknown shard must error for any replica")
+}

+
+
+class ScriptedConnection(ConnectionHandler):
+
+
+    def __init__(self, raw_voltage_sums):
+        self._raw_voltage_sums = list(raw_voltage_sums)
+        self.writes = []
+
+    def connect(self):
+        return None
+
+    def disconnect(self):
+        return None
+
+    def write(self, data):
+        self.writes.append(bytes(data))
+        return len(data)
+
+    def read(self, numbytes):
+        if numbytes == 1:
+            return b"\x01"
+        if numbytes == 2:
+            return self._raw_voltage_sums.pop(0).to_bytes(2, "little")
+        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected read size: {numbytes}")
+
+
+class UnreadableMeasurementConnection(ScriptedConnection):
+    def read(self, numbytes):
+        if numbytes == 1:
+            return b"\x01"
+        if numbytes == 2:
+            raise ConnectionError("device not connected")
+        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected read size: {numbytes}")

+	writeFilterFile(t, columnsRoot, "!secret\n@nested.rules\n")
+	writeFilterFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "columns", "nested.rules"), "secret\n")
+	cf, err := filter.ParseColumnFilter([]string{"@" + columnsRoot})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.True(t, cf.MatchColumn("secret"))
+	require.False(t, cf.MatchColumn("other"))

+	writeFilterFile(t, b, "@../a.rules\n")
+
+	_, err := filter.Parse([]string{"@" + a})
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.Contains(t, strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "cycle")

+func TestConfigAuditScannerScanResolvesDeploymentOwnerBeforeBuildingScanJob(t *testing.T) {
+	deploy := scannerOwnerDeployment("config-owner", corev1.NamespaceDefault, "7")
+	activeRS := scannerOwnerReplicaSet("config-owner-rs", corev1.NamespaceDefault, "7")
+	kubeClient := ctrlfake.NewClientBuilder().
+		WithScheme(starboard.NewScheme()).
+		WithObjects(deploy, activeRS).
+		Build()
+	plugin := &recordingConfigAuditPlugin{err: errors.New("stop before running scan job")}
+	pluginContext := starboard.NewPluginContext().
+		WithName("owner-test").
+		WithNamespace(starboard.NamespaceName).
+		WithClient(kubeClient).
+		WithServiceAccountName(starboard.ServiceAccountName).
+		Get()
+	scanner := configauditreport.NewScanner(
+		k8sfake.NewSimpleClientset(),
+		kubeClient,
+		plugin,
+		pluginContext,
+		starboard.ConfigData{},
+		kube.ScannerOpts{},
+	)
+
+	_, err := scanner.Scan(context.Background(), kube.Object{
+		Kind:      kube.KindDeployment,
+		Name:      deploy.Name,
+		Namespace: deploy.Namespace,
+	})
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, plugin.seenObject)
+	assert.Equal(t, string(kube.KindReplicaSet), plugin.seenObject.GetObjectKind().GroupVersionKind().Kind)
+	assert.Equal(t, activeRS.Name, plugin.seenObject.GetName())
+	assert.Equal(t, activeRS.Namespace, plugin.seenObject.GetNamespace())

format-code-task-000177.build_env_cmd:
cd /testbed

# Activate virtual environment
source /testbed/.venv/bin/activate

# Start PostgreSQL if not running
service postgresql start 2>/dev/null || true

# Build addons path with all OCA repos
ADDONS_PATH="/testbed/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/odoo/addons"
ADDONS_PATH="$ADDONS_PATH,/testbed"
for d in /testbed/account-financial-tools /testbed/account-invoicing /testbed/account-payment /testbed/account-reconcile /testbed/bank-payment /testbed/brand /testbed/commission /testbed/contract /testbed/currency /testbed/manufacture /testbed/mis-builder /testbed/product-attribute /testbed/purchase-workflow /testbed/sale-workflow /testbed/web /testbed/delivery-carrier; do
    if [ -d "$d" ]; then
        ADDONS_PATH="$ADDONS_PATH,$d"
    fi
done

# Drop and recreate test database
dropdb -h /var/run/postgresql -p 5433 test_wh 2>/dev/null || true
createdb -h /var/run/postgresql -p 5433 test_wh 2>&1

# Run the test for l10n_br_account_withholding
odoo -d test_wh \
    --addons-path="$ADDONS_PATH" \
    -i l10n_br_account_withholding,l10n_br_sale_commission \
    --test-enable \
    --test-tags=/l10n_br_account_withholding \
    --stop-after-init \
    --log-level=test \
    --no-http \
    --db_host=/var/run/postgresql \
    --db_port=5433 2>&1
TEST_EXIT=$?

# Clean up
dropdb -h /var/run/postgresql -p 5433 test_wh 2>/dev/null || true

exit $TEST_EXIT

}

assert_file_lines_unordered() {
    local file=$1 expected=$2 label=$3
    [ -f "$file" ] || fail "$label: missing $file"
    local actual_sorted expected_sorted

    expected_sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "$expected" | LC_ALL=C sort)
    [ "$actual_sorted" = "$expected_sorted" ] || fail "$label: got sorted [$actual_sorted], want sorted [$expected_sorted]"

    [ ! -e "$file" ] || fail "$label: expected no executed scenarios, got [$(cat "$file")]"

assert_err_has() {
    local pattern=$1 file=$2 label=$3
    grep -qE "$pattern" "$file" || fail "$label: stderr did not match $pattern; got [$(cat "$file")]"
}

assert_output_lacks() {
    local pattern=$1 label=$2
    ! grep -qE "$pattern" out err || fail "$label: output unexpectedly matched $pattern; stdout [$(cat out)] stderr [$(cat err)]"
}

assert_name_not_reported_missing() {

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Callable
+
+import pytest
+
+from marimo._utils.file_watcher import FileWatcher
+
+
+async def _wait_for(
+    condition: Callable[[], bool], timeout: float = 5.0
+) -> bool:
+
+    elapsed = 0.0
+    step = 0.02
+    while elapsed < timeout:
+        if condition():
+            return True
+        await asyncio.sleep(step)
+        elapsed += step
+    return condition()
+
+
+def _touch_with_new_mtime(path: Path) -> None:
+
+    with open(path, "a") as f:
+        f.write("# changed\n")
+    stat = os.stat(path)
+    os.utime(path, (stat.st_atime + 10, stat.st_mtime + 10))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_callback_invoked_on_modification(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    target = tmp_path / "notebook.py"
+    target.write_text("x = 1\n")
+
+    calls: list[Path] = []
+
+    async def on_change(path: Path) -> None:
+        calls.append(path)
+
+    watcher = FileWatcher.create(target, on_change)
+    try:
+        watcher.start()
+
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
+        _touch_with_new_mtime(target)
+        assert await _wait_for(lambda: len(calls) >= 1)
+    finally:
+        watcher.stop()
+
+    assert len(calls) >= 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_callback_receives_watched_path(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    target = tmp_path / "app.py"
+    target.write_text("y = 2\n")
+
+    received: list[Path] = []
+
+    async def on_change(path: Path) -> None:
+        received.append(path)
+
+    watcher = FileWatcher.create(target, on_change)
+    try:
+        watcher.start()
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
+        _touch_with_new_mtime(target)
+        assert await _wait_for(lambda: len(received) >= 1)
+    finally:
+        watcher.stop()
+
+    assert Path(received[0]) == target
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_no_callback_when_unmodified(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    target = tmp_path / "stable.py"
+    target.write_text("z = 3\n")
+
+    calls: list[Path] = []
+
+    async def on_change(path: Path) -> None:
+        calls.append(path)
+
+    watcher = FileWatcher.create(target, on_change)
+    try:
+        watcher.start()
+
+        await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
+    finally:
+        watcher.stop()
+
+    assert calls == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_multiple_modifications_trigger_multiple_callbacks(
+    tmp_path: Path,
+) -> None:
+    target = tmp_path / "multi.py"
+    target.write_text("a = 0\n")
+
+    calls: list[Path] = []
+
+    async def on_change(path: Path) -> None:
+        calls.append(path)
+
+    watcher = FileWatcher.create(target, on_change)
+    try:
+        watcher.start()
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
+
+        _touch_with_new_mtime(target)
+        assert await _wait_for(lambda: len(calls) >= 1)
+
+        _touch_with_new_mtime(target)
+        assert await _wait_for(lambda: len(calls) >= 2)
+    finally:
+        watcher.stop()
+
+    assert len(calls) >= 2
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_stop_halts_callbacks(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    target = tmp_path / "stopme.py"
+    target.write_text("b = 1\n")
+
+    calls: list[Path] = []
+
+    async def on_change(path: Path) -> None:
+        calls.append(path)
+
+    watcher = FileWatcher.create(target, on_change)
+    watcher.start()
+    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
+    _touch_with_new_mtime(target)
+    assert await _wait_for(lambda: len(calls) >= 1)
+
+    watcher.stop()
+
+    await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
+    count_after_stop = len(calls)
+
+    _touch_with_new_mtime(target)
+    await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
+
+    assert len(calls) == count_after_stop

--- a/flocker/control/test/test_httpapi.py
+++ b/flocker/control/test/test_httpapi.py
@@ -173,6 +173,304 @@ RealTestsAPI, MemoryTestsAPI = buildIntegrationTests(
     VersionTestsMixin, "API", _build_app)
 
 
+class CreateContainerTestsMixin(APITestsMixin):
+    """
+    Black-box tests for creating container configuration through the HTTP API.
+    """
+    def _request_json(self, method, path, body, expected_code):
+        """
+        Issue a JSON request through the existing HTTP API test harness and
+        return a ``Deferred`` firing with the decoded response body.
+
+        This helper intentionally does not inspect route handlers, decorators,
+        schemas, or private helpers.
+        """
+        requesting = self.assertResponseCode(
+            method, path, body, expected_code)
+        requesting.addCallback(readBody)
+        requesting.addCallback(loads)
+        return requesting
+
+    def _applications_for_host(self, host):
+        """
+        Return the configured applications for ``host`` from the persisted
+        configuration.
+        """
+        deployment = self.persistence_service.get()
+        matching = [
+            node for node in deployment.nodes
+            if node.hostname == host
+        ]
+        if not matching:
+            return []
+        return list(matching[0].applications)
+
+    def _configured_applications_named(self, name):
+        """
+        Return all configured applications with the supplied public container
+        name, across all hosts.
+        """
+        deployment = self.persistence_service.get()
+        return [
+            application
+            for node in deployment.nodes
+            for application in node.applications
+            if application.name == name
+        ]
+
+    def _assert_application_present(self, host, name, image):
+        """
+        Assert that the persisted configuration contains a container with the
+        supplied public values on ``host``.
+        """
+        expected_image = DockerImage.from_string(image)
+        matches = [
+            application for application in self._applications_for_host(host)
+            if application.name == name and application.image == expected_image
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            len(matches), 1,
+            "Expected exactly one configured container named {!r} with image "
+            "{!r} on host {!r}; found {!r}".format(
+                name, image, host, self._applications_for_host(host)))
+
+    def _assert_duplicate_name_conflict(self, response_json):
+        """
+        Assert only the public error shape and duplicate-name semantics.
+        The exact prose is intentionally not locked down because the reference
+        patch's docs and implementation disagree on the full sentence.
+        """
+
+
+        self.assertIn(u"description", response_json)
+        self.assertNotIn(u"message", response_json)
+        self.assertTrue(isinstance(response_json[u"description"], unicode))
+        self.assertTrue(response_json[u"description"])
+
+    def test_create_container_response_echoes_request(self):
+        """
+        Creating a container returns 201 Created and echoes the public
+        host/name/image values from the request body.
+        """
+        container_json = {
+            u"host": self.NODE_B,
+            u"name": u"postgres",
+            u"image": u"postgres",
+        }
+        return self.assertResult(
+            b"POST", b"/configuration/containers",
+            container_json, CREATED, container_json)
+
+    def test_create_container_persists_on_requested_existing_host(self):
+        """
+        Creating a container on an existing host persists it on that host and
+        preserves unrelated existing configuration.
+        """
+        saving = self.persistence_service.save(Deployment(
+            nodes={
+                Node(
+                    hostname=self.NODE_A,
+                    applications=[
+                        Application(
+                            name=u"postgres",
+                            image=DockerImage.from_string(u"postgres")),
+                    ]),
+                Node(hostname=self.NODE_B),
+            }))
+
+        def saved(_):
+            return self.assertResponseCode(
+                b"POST", b"/configuration/containers",
+                {
+                    u"host": self.NODE_A,
+                    u"name": u"another_postgres",
+                    u"image": u"postgres:latest",
+                },
+                CREATED)
+        saving.addCallback(saved)
+
+        def created(_):
+            self._assert_application_present(
+                self.NODE_A, u"postgres", u"postgres")
+            self._assert_application_present(
+                self.NODE_A, u"another_postgres", u"postgres:latest")
+            self.assertEqual(
+                [],
+                [
+                    application for application
+                    in self._applications_for_host(self.NODE_B)
+                    if application.name == u"another_postgres"
+                ])
+        saving.addCallback(created)
+        return saving
+
+    def test_create_container_persists_on_new_host(self):
+        """
+        Creating a container for a host absent from the current configuration
+        persists a host entry containing that container.
+        """
+        d = self.assertResponseCode(
+            b"POST", b"/configuration/containers",
+            {
+                u"host": self.NODE_B,
+                u"name": u"redis_cache",
+                u"image": u"redis:latest",
+            },
+            CREATED)
+
+        def created(_):
+            self._assert_application_present(
+                self.NODE_B, u"redis_cache", u"redis:latest")
+        d.addCallback(created)
+        return d
+
+    d

+import sys

+

+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+
+sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/repo")
+
+from lib.models import LightFC
+
+
+def _ns(**kwargs):
+    return SimpleNamespace(**kwargs)
+
+
+def _cfg(
+    backbone_type="MobileNetV2",
+    inplanes=192,
+    freeze_bn=False,
+    num_kernel=64,
+    adj_channel=96,
+    channel=256,
+    feat_sz=16,
+    stride=16,
+):
+    return _ns(
+        MODEL=_ns(
+            BACKBONE=_ns(
+                TYPE=backbone_type,
+                USE_PRETRAINED=False,
+                PRETRAIN_FILE=None,
+                LOAD_MODE=1,
+            ),
+            FUSION=_ns(PARAMS=_ns(num_kernel=num_kernel, adj_channel=adj_channel)),
+            HEAD=_ns(
+                PARAMS=_ns(
+                    inplanes=inplanes,
+                    channel=channel,
+                    feat_sz=feat_sz,
+                    stride=stride,
+                    freeze_bn=freeze_bn,
+                )
+            ),
+        )
+    )
+
+
+class RecordingBackbone(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def forward(self, tensor):
+        call_number = len(self.calls) + 1
+        self.calls.append((tuple(tensor.shape), float(tensor.sum())))
+        return tensor + (10.0 * call_number)
+
+
+class RecordingFusion(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def forward(self, z_feat, x_feat):
+        self.calls.append((float(z_feat.sum()), float(x_feat.sum())))
+        return z_feat + x_feat
+
+
+class RecordingHead(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def forward(self, fused):
+        fused_sum = float(fused.sum())
+        self.calls.append(fused_sum)
+        return {
+            "marker": torch.tensor([fused_sum], dtype=torch.float32),
+            "shape": tuple(fused.shape),
+        }
+
+
+def _install_recorders(net):
+    net.backbone = RecordingBackbone()
+    net.fusion = RecordingFusion()
+    net.head = RecordingHead()
+    return net
+
+

+    if torch.is_tensor(expected):
+        assert torch.is_tensor(actual)
+        assert actual.shape == expected.shape
+        assert torch.allclose(actual, expected)

      npx genversion --semi "$pkg/lib/version.js" 2>/dev/null
    fi

run_database_jest() {

+    candidates = [normalize_job_id(message) for message in miss_messages(logger) if task_name in message]

+def test_dryrun_logs_existing_task_called_with_new_arguments(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+
+
+
+

+        return 1
+
+    def workload_out(self):
+        return 1
+
+
+class WorkloadHW:
+    def __init__(self, workload_in, workload_out):
+        self._workload_in = workload_in
+        self._workload_out = workload_out
+
+    def workload_in(self):
+        return self._workload_in
+
+    def workload_out(self):
+        return self._workload_out
+
+
+class ConfiguredPartition:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name,
+        workload_in,
+        workload_out,
+        batch_size,
+        wr_factor,
+        cycle,
+        interval,
+        pipeline_depth,
+    ):
+        self.name = name
+        self.input_nodes = [f"{name}_in"]
+        self.output_nodes = [f"{name}_out"]
+        self.batch_size = batch_size
+        self.wr_factor = wr_factor
+        self._cycle = cycle
+        self._interval = interval
+        self._pipeline_depth = pipeline_depth
+        self.graph = nx.DiGraph()
+        self.graph.add_node(self.input_nodes[0], hw=WorkloadHW(workload_in, 0))
+        self.graph.add_node(self.output_nodes[0], hw=WorkloadHW(0, workload_out))
+        self.graph.add_edge(self.input_nodes[0], self.output_nodes[0])
+
+    def get_cycle(self):
+        return self._cycle
+
+    def get_interval(self):
+        return self._interval
+
+    def get_pipeline_depth(self):
+        return self._pipeline_depth
+
+
+def make_network(batch_size=4):
+    graph = nx.DiGraph()
+    graph.add_node(
+        "bootstrap",
+        type=LAYER_TYPE.NOP,
+        hw=BootstrapHW(),
+        onnx_node=None,
+        onnx_input=[],
+        onnx_output=[],
+    )
+    network = Network("acceptance", model=None, graph=graph, batch_size=batch_size)
+    network.multi_fpga = False
+    return network
+
+
+def configured_network(batch_size=4):
+    network = make_network(batch_size=batch_size)
+    network.partitions = [

+        ConfiguredPartition("p1", 25, 30, 1, 2, 200, 35, 7),
+        ConfiguredPartition("p2", 4, 9, 3, 1, 50, 12, 11),
+    ]
+    return network
+
+
+def partition_state(network):
+    return [

+            partition.batch_size,
+            partition.wr_factor,
+            partition._cycle,
